To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Mob1 and the chromosomal passenger protein complex mutually depend on each other for localization during mitosis.

Mob1 is essential for mitotic progression in Drosophila melanogaster, and is required for the proper localization of Aurora B and INCENP at the spindle midzone in early anaphase, and for the recruitment of NudC to the spindle mid-zone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Mob1 and its interaction with the chromosomal passenger protein complex in regulating cytokinesis.
the role of Mob1 in the regulation of cytokinesis in metazoans.
the role of the chromosomal protein H2A.Z in gene regulation and chromatin structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chromosomal passenger protein, INCENP, is essential for the localization of Mob1 during mitosis and that Mob1 is essential for the recruitment of INCENP to the spindle mid-zone.
Mob1 and the CPC are functionally linked and mutually depend on each other to regulate mitosis.
the chromosomal passenger protein complex is a complex consisting of Aurora B, survivin, INCENP and Borealin, which are required for chromosome alignment, segregation and cytokinesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Mob1 and the chromosomal passenger proteins are mutually dependent for localization during mitosis.

Mob1 facilitates mitosis and cytokinesis through two distinct mechanisms: 1) through its interaction with the NDR kinase Cdr2 to regulate the timing of mitotic exit; and 2) through its interaction the chromosomal passenger protein Eg5 to regulate cytokinesis.

Mob1 is essential for the recruitment of Aurora B to the spindle mid-zone, and the absence of this kinase results in the mis-localization of other components of the chromosomal complex to the mid-zone, including Survivin and INCENP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Mob1 is an essential regulator for the recruitment of a mitosis-specific protein complex to the mitotic spindle midzone.
Mob1 and Aurora B are mutually dependent for localization to the mitotic spindle.
Mob1 and the chromosomal passenger proteins are mutually dependent for localization during early anaphage.
